newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to reduce state ownership in smaller banks.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to reduce state ownership in smaller banks.

text.p: New financial legislation put forward by Hungary on Thursday would reduce the maximum stake the state can hold in a bank to 15 percent from 25 percent for banks which have less than a 25 percent market share in any one banking sector.

Agnes Balazs, Deputy State Secretary at the Finance Ministry, told a news conference on Friday that only OTP has a large enough market share to be allowed a larger than 15 percent state-owned stake. @

However, in the future other banks could also achieve a large enough market share in one of the sectors outlined in the bill, which would include personal deposits and lending, corporate and municipal accounts, she added.
OTP is Hungary's largest commercial bank by virtue of its nationwide network and its role as the leading banker for individuals and muncipalities.
The new ruling, which is to lower the limit of state-owned stakes in banks, could also lead to a partial sale of the state's 25-percent holding in OTP, experts said. @

"This creates ground for a transaction," said Istvan Abel, managing director of the state privatisation APV, in answer to a question adding, however, that APV has not worked out any plans about the sale of further OTP shares.
Hungary would also need to modify the privatisation law before reducing its stake in OTP, an OTP official said.
